notices.short_title: Fire & Safety Inspection Services for DVPHA housing
notices.description: The Adult Protective Services (APS) Division of Voluntary and Proprietary Homes for Adults (DVPHA), which operates two state-mandated housing programs that utilize private housing as licensed residences. They are the Family-type Homes for Adults (FTHA) and the Foster Family Care Program (FFCP). Fire safety inspections for homes used by these programs are required by New York State regulations concerning eligibility for an operating license. The New York City Human Resources Administration and Adult Protective services have the responsibility for supervision of these programs. The lowest bidder, Pyramid Safety and Health Solution, Inc is our current vendor. They have been providing fire and safety inspection services to the clients over six (6) years. They are very responsive and responsible to the program. Their bid price is fair and reasonable. Contract budget: $47,760 Contract term: 7/1/2026 - 6/30/2029 PIN: 26ZSEAP01101
notices.plain: The Human Resources Administration awarded Pyramid Safety & Health Solutions Inc a $47,760 contract, through a small purchase from a certified minority- or women-owned business without competition, for fire safety inspections of licensed family-type and foster family care homes for adults from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2029.

notices.description: The Department of Design and Construction is seeking a Special Inspector to provide special inspection services for the LNXA20WKF - Wakefield Library ADA Renovation - Special Inspections project. notices.short_title: COMPASS Programs in Public Schools - Middle
notices.description:
COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs.
